::: {#rem-symmetric-antisymmetric}
#### Antisymmetric is not the opposite of symmetric

A relation can be symmetric (@def-symmetric-relation) and antisymmetric (@def-antisymmetric),
only one of the two,
or neither:

- the relation $\set{(\text{cow}, \text{cow}), (\text{dog}, \text{dog})}$ on $V$ is both,
  since it relates no word to a different word, so no pair can break either property;
- the relation $T$ of @exm-shares-letter is symmetric but not antisymmetric;
- the relation $B$ of @exm-beats is antisymmetric but not symmetric;
- the relation $\set{(\text{cat}, \text{cow}), (\text{cow}, \text{cat}), (\text{dog}, \text{pig})}$ on $V$ is neither:
  it relates cat and cow both ways, so it is not antisymmetric,
  and it has $(\text{dog}, \text{pig})$ but not $(\text{pig}, \text{dog})$, so it is not symmetric.

A relation with both properties never relates two different elements:
if $a \mathrel{R} b$, then $b \mathrel{R} a$ by symmetry, and then $a = b$ by antisymmetry.
So "not symmetric" and "antisymmetric" say different things.
A relation is not symmetric when one pair $(a, b)$ in it has its reverse $(b, a)$ missing,
while it is antisymmetric when no two different elements are related both ways.

:::
